And Counsel for Applicant :- Deo Prakash Srivastava Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Karunesh Singh Pawar,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned A.G.A. for the State as well as perused the record.

The present bail application has been filed by accused-applicant seeking bail in Case Crime No.223 of 2023, under Sections 363, 366, 376 IPC, Sections 51, 6, 5n of the POCSO Act, P.S. Katra Bazar,
District Gonda.
In the F.I.R., it is alleged that minor daughter of the informant aged about 13 years went somewhere from home along with her aadhar card.

1 Learned counsel for the applicant submits that victim in her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. has stated that she on her own accord went away with the applicant and resided with him in Ludhiyana.
She has levelled allegation of rape against the applicant in her statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C.
In the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., she has stated that she without informing anybody at home went with the applicant and stay with him in Ludhiyana for a period of 10 days.

He further submits that radiological age of the victim is 18-19 years, she was a consenting party and at no point of time she raised alarm although she travelled with the applicant right up to Ludhiyana and stayed there 10 days.
There was ample opportunity to raise the alarm but she has not done.
Medical does not support the prosecution case.
No corroborative evidence has been found, in the medical examination of the victim.
It is lastly submitted that mother of the victim namely, Geeta Devi has been examined.
She has not supported the prosecution case while giving statement as P.W.1.
Learned A.G.A. has opposed the bail prayer and has submitted that as per the school record, the age of the victim is 14 years, 3 months and 10 days.
Rebutting the same, learned counsel for the applicant submits that age of the minor has to be ascertained in trial.
He has placed reliance on the judgment of Co-ordinate Bench of this Court delivered on 09.02.2023 in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.55026 of 2021 (Monish vs. State).

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.55026 of 2021 (Monish vs. State)

sentences.text: On due consideration to the submissions advanced, perusal of the record as also the fact that the applicant is languishing in jail since 26.05.2023, applicant has no criminal history, statement of P.W.1 so also the statement of the victim recorded under Sections 161 & 164 Cr.P.C. and the medical examination report, without expressing any opinion on merits of the case I find it to be a fit case for enlarging the applicant on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant Om Prakash be released on bail in aforesaid case crime number subject to his furnishing a personal bond and two reliable sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial court concerned with the following conditions:
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
(ii) The applicant will not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.
(iii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iv) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as Om Prakash vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ...

In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(vi) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation,
